# Candidate module designs
- Module-D1: large-area light guide with thin bonded dichroic filter.
- Module-D3: wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout.
- Module-D2: compact SiPM tile array.

# Earlier simulation summary (2025, 20% coverage)
Light collection: Module-D1 38 PE/MeV, Module-D3 27 PE/MeV, Module-D2 18 PE/MeV. It rises with coverage, roughly as coverage^0.8.

# Thermal-cycling tests
Batches of 40 modules of each design were cycled 20 times between 300 K and 87 K.
Fraction failed (open channels or delamination):
- Module-D1: 30%  (the thin light-guide bonding cracks on cooldown)
- Module-D3: 2%
- Module-D2: 0.5%
Requirement: at most 5% failures after 20 cycles.

# Meeting notes 2026-01-20
Cabling feedthroughs were reviewed; enough feedthroughs are available for up to 30% coverage.

content.text: D1 fails thermal cycling at 30% (over the 5% limit), so it's out. D3 (2%) and D2 (0.5%) both pass. I'll simulate both at maximum allowed coverage to compare light yield.

input.justification: Module-D1 has the highest light yield on paper (38 PE/MeV at 20% in the 2025 summary), but its thin bonded light guide fails 30% of modules after 20 thermal cycles, far above the 5% hard limit, and failed modules cannot be replaced. Module-D2 passes thermal cycling (0.5%) but gives only ~23.9 PE/MeV at 30% coverage. Module-D3 passes thermal cycling (2% failed, from the test batch) and gives 37.0 PE/MeV at 30% coverage in the Geant4 simulation, the highest light collection among the compliant designs. 30% is the top of the allowed coverage range, and the meeting notes confirm enough feedthroughs exist for 30% coverage. Light yield rises with coverage, so 30% is the best choice within constraints.
